target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter second-collection writer (sub_080119BC)
target.role: keyed replace in the first collection, else remove the key from the second and append to the first
target.notes: sub_080119BC, the routine that reaches the SECOND collection as a writer. THE WRITE CONTRACT: it scans the FIRST collection FORWARD from index 0 comparing each element against the KEY (second argument). If the key is found, it REPLACES that element with the value and does NOT touch any count. If the key is absent from the first collection it scans the SECOND collection the same way at object + 0x40C, and when the key is found there it REMOVES it through sub_0804FE54(object + 0x408, index), then APPENDS the value to the FIRST collection, incrementing only the first collection's count. So it is a keyed MOVE ACROSS THE TWO COLLECTIONS. THE SECOND COLLECTION IS A WRITER TARGET ONLY THROUGH THAT REMOVAL: nothing here appends to it and nothing here increments its count. THE SECOND COLLECTION IS REACHED BY A COMPUTED BASE, NOT A DISPLACEMENT: the routine adds 0x40C to the object base once and works through that register afterwards, which is why an image-wide search for stores at a displacement near 0x40C finds NOTHING. That also explains why the count it reads is at object + 0x40C and the elements at object + 0x410 + 4*i, the shape the reader sub_08011C70 proved. ORDER: both scans run FORWARD, so the FIRST element equal to the key wins, the OPPOSITE direction from the reader's backward search. The value is stored VERBATIM. NO CAPACITY CHECK and no bounds check. +0x00 IS NOT TOUCHED. COMPARISON WITH sub_0801191A, and this is measured rather than inferred from their adjacency: they are NOT structurally equivalent at different offsets. sub_0801191A is a GENERIC append that takes any collection base, and its callers pass many different bases including *(r5+4), *(r5) and *(r7+0xc), so it is not tied to this object or to either of its collections. sub_080119BC hardcodes the 0x40C offset and knows about both of this object's collections. They are two members of ONE API FAMILY with DIFFERENT roles: a generic append, and an object-specific keyed move. UNKNOWN: what the elements mean, what sub_0804FE54 does beyond removing an entry and whether it compacts, and CRUCIALLY WHAT APPENDS TO THE SECOND COLLECTION - this routine only removes from it, so the second collection's INSERTION path is still unfound. The object's +0x00 field is untouched here. No semantic name is assigned and nothing is imported from another title.
